chapter: Road shows in the Southwest and Midwest
title: Hattie McDaniel joins the Spikes show from the Nat Reece carnival
summary: Hattie McDaniel and her brother left Nat Reece's carnival in Douglas and were featured with the Spikes Brothers; Spikes later saw her preparing for Gone With The Wind.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Oh, I don't remember. We bought uniforms--sent off and got uniforms from the uniform stores, you know. I think some of them--some of the uniforms was khaki. You know, soldiers' khaki and thing...but it's been so long that... I had a picture of them--the whole band and everything--but I can't find where they are. I got a lot of junk stored away in the basement but I guess it's all down there. Even when I was drafted in Honolulu to go in the Army in the big band there was...I'm a saxophone player and clarinet player but when I went in the Army, I took up trombone and played slide trombone in the band, and I got all those pictures but I don't know where they are. Anyway, we had this little troupe, and one of the stars in those days was Hattie McDaniels. She...We picked her up, and she come through there with a troupe or show called Nat Reece Carnival. Her and her brother and family and we took her away from Nat Reece and she went...uh...came to us, and we featured her for a coupla years with our show called Spikes Brothers'...uh, what is that? Novelty Stars or something? And we used to make this little circuit, and she was with us a couple of terms around, and then she went back to Denver
to her home, and the next time I saw Hattie, she was in California, and she was getting ready to do "Gone With The Wind."
How old was Hattie when she worked with you?
Oh, about sixteen or seventeen. Just almost my age, I guess. No, I was...let's see, Hattie's about eight...I was about twenty, I guess--nineteen or twenty.
It was in what city that you met Hattie?

She come through with Nat Reece in Douglas, Arizona, and her brother. Her brother was with Nat Reece, and his wife. They came through there, and they left the show. They were dissatisfied, and they came over with us.
The Nat Reece Show was what? Just a variety show?

No, Nat Reece was a carnival. From Kansas. Yes, they went out every year, just like Ringling Bros., only they... you know, they had the merry-go-rounds and all the shows and the big tent and everything--just like a regular...well, you know what a carnival is.
